Method of Attack: Exploiting data deletion capabilities of endpoint detection and response (EDR) and antivirus (AV) software to turn them into data wipers
Using time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerability with Windows junctions to redirect deletion commands to critical system files
Creating a malicious file held open to postpone deletion until reboot, then deleting files by following junctions blindly during reboot
Bypassing ransomware protection features like Controlled Folder Access by abusing trusted EDR/AV deletion privileges
Attack Vector: Abuse of legitimate EDR and AV file deletion/quarantine mechanisms
Use of Windows junctions to redirect deletion to protected system files
Triggering deletion commands scheduled for reboot via PendingFileRenameOperations registry
Indicators of Compromise: Use of junction from C:\Temp to C:\Windows
Malicious file named ndis.sys placed in C:\temp\Windows\System32\drivers
PendingFileRenameOperations registry entries causing file deletion on reboot
